_readme: Pages the weekly HSK watch checks. Edit freely: see docs/HSK-WATCH.md. 'verified' is only a note for humans (set it to true once you have seen the source succeed in a real run); the script ignores it. Optional per-source keys: enabled (false = skip), links (false = ignore link addresses), minChars (default 200), ignore (list of regular expressions; matching lines are dropped).

sources.name: Chinese Testing International: home page
sources.why: Official HSK organiser. The home page links to the current year's test calendar and the pinned announcement, so a new calendar or announcement shows up here as a changed link.

sources.name: Chinese Testing International: HSK overview (HSK 3.0, 'three stages, nine levels')
sources.why: Official description of the HSK and of the move to HSK 3.0: links to the new syllabus, sample questions and the demo test.

sources.name: Chinese Testing International: HSK level 4 format
sources.why: The level this app prepares for: number of questions, sections, duration, pass mark. A change here means the level 4 exam format changed.

sources.name: Chinese Testing International: news and notices list
sources.why: Official announcements. May be drawn by JavaScript, in which case a plain download sees only the menu (the run log will say 'same text as cti-home').

sources.name: Chinese Testing International: 2026 test calendar
sources.why: Exam dates for 2026. Replace the URL each year with the new calendar link from the home page. May be drawn by JavaScript or be an image (see cti-news).

sources.name: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (CLEC, formerly Hanban)
sources.why: The Ministry of Education body that owns the HSK and publishes policy news about it. URL written from memory.

sources.name: Ministry of Education: Chinese Proficiency Grading Standards (basis of HSK 3.0)
sources.why: The national standard (GF 0025-2021) that HSK 3.0 implements. Rarely changes; a change would be important. URL written from memory.
